# Ecomify Insights Dashboard  
Real-time analytics for e-commerce KPIs and customer behavior tracking. Built for production use, this dashboard aggregates data from multiple sources to provide actionable insights for growth strategies.  

## Badges  
[![Production Ready](https://via.placeholder.com/150/4CAF50)](https://example.com) | [![AWS Integration](https://via.placeholder.com/150/2196F3)](https://example.com) | [![Kubernetes Deployed](https://via.placeholder.com/150/FFC107)](https://example.com)  

## Getting Started / Installation  
Clone the repository and install dependencies:  
```bash  
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/ecomify.git  
cd ecomify  
npm install  
```  
Set environment variables for AWS credentials, database connections, and API keys. Deploy using Docker or directly on AWS ECS.  

## Tech Stack  
- **Frontend**: React.js with Chart.js for dynamic visualizations  
- **Backend**: Node.js with Express for real-time data streaming  
- **Database**: PostgreSQL (optimized with indexing and connection pooling) + Redis for caching  
- **Cloud**: AWS Lambda for serverless processing, S3 for storage  
- **Monitoring**: Prometheus + Grafana for system metrics  

## Architecture / Design  
The dashboard uses a microservices architecture with event sourcing for KPI aggregation. AWS Lambda processes raw data into structured metrics, which are then ingested into PostgreSQL. Redis caches frequent queries to reduce database load. Kubernetes manages container orchestration, while Terraform provisions infrastructure as code. Cloud cost optimization focuses on auto-scaling and spot instances for batch processing. Technical debt was addressed by refactoring legacy data pipelines into modular services.  

## Usage / Examples  
Run the app with:  
```bash  
npm start  
```  
Access the dashboard at `http://localhost:3000`. Example metrics include:  
- Real-time conversion rates  
- Customer session duration trends  
- Product category performance  

## Testing  
Unit tests (Jest) cover core logic, while integration tests validate data flow between services. End-to-end tests (Cypress) simulate user interactions. CI/CD pipelines automate testing and deployment via GitHub Actions.
